# SB-1021 Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-SB03

Hazard description
------------------

An arc flash event occurred adjacent to the induction power cabinet that supplies the Hot Forge induction heaters. Investigation identified interaction between a dust collector alarm condition and maintenance activity at the nearby shot blast cabinet ventilation plenum as a credible contributor to an unusual transient on the local electrical distribution. The immediate hazard is thermal and blast energy from an electrical arc, with potential for severe injury and equipment damage. Secondary hazards include ignition of combustible dust, exposure to metal fragments, and interruption of critical controls for forging operations.

Root cause analysis identified an uncontrolled dust collector pressure drop alarm condition on the shot blast cabinet ventilation that coincided with a planned maintenance activity at the induction power cabinet. The dust handling condition is documented as follows: The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 1240 Pa. That alarm threshold and the cabinet identifier are relevant to sequencing of work and to permit conditions.

Affected equipment
------------------

This bulletin applies to the induction power cabinet and associated feeder switchgear serving the Hot Forge induction heaters in plant P2, line P2-L1. It specifically references the shot blast dust collection system feeding cabinet EQ-P2-L1-SB03 and any auxiliary ventilation or interlock panels that share local control circuits or common fusing. Personnel who perform activities on or near the induction power cabinet, the shot blast cabinet ventilation plenum, or the dust collector should consider the conditions described here before entry.

Required controls
-----------------

Engineering and administrative controls must be applied immediately to reduce arc flash risk when work is planned or underway in the area described above.

- Prework verification: Before any maintenance, testing, or cleaning at the induction power cabinet or at the adjacent shot blast cabinet ventilation, verify alarm states and dust collector pressure readings using the site control system and physical inspection of the collector differential gauge. Confirm that the dust collector pressure drop alarm state is not active. The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 1240 Pa; treat any alarm condition matching that descriptor as a stop condition for electrical work until resolved.

- Work sequencing: Coordinate electrical isolation and lockout procedures with ventilation maintenance. If dust collector alarms are present, do not energize or reenergize cabinet power until alarms are cleared and interlocks are confirmed stable. Maintain clear communication between the electrical crew and the ventilation maintenance lead. Use the communication procedure in SOP-P2-L1-01 for coordination of multi-discipline work.

- Hazard mitigation: Apply electrically safe work practices per the established arc flash program. Where deenergized maintenance is not practicable, treat the cabinet as live and use appropriate personal protective equipment for energized work. Limit personnel in the arc flash boundary to authorized, trained individuals. Use insulated tools and maintain grounding continuity for portable grounded equipment.

- Controls verification: After any change to ventilation or dust collector status, perform post-change verification of control interlocks, protective relays, and cabinet door microswitches before permitting energized operations. Record verification actions in the maintenance log and reference ECN-2026-036 for any recent engineering changes that could affect local interlocks.

- Training and permits: Require a documented prejob brief and an energized work permit when work involves potential exposure to arc flash. Include a line item to check the dust collector alarm state for EQ-P2-L1-SB03. Use SOP-P2-L1-03 for electrical isolation and lockout-tagout detail during permits that include induction power components.

Implementation rationale and examples
------------------------------------

The dust collector alarm value is an operational indicator of abnormal airflow or filter loading at the shot blast cabinet. When the alarm threshold shown above is reached, airflow transients and local control responses can create unintended sequences in shared control cabinets. For example, a maintenance crew replacing filters on the shot blast cabinet can momentarily change the load on the collector fan, which may cause an auxiliary contact to change state and initiate a temporary undervoltage or relay chase. If electrical work is in progress at the induction power cabinet at the same time, transient relay operations can allow a phase to reenergize or close a breaker unexpectedly. Coordinating work and ensuring alarms are cleared prevents overlapping events that increase arc flash likelihood.

Records to keep
----------------

Maintain the following records for each work activity affected by this bulletin:

- Prework verification checklist that includes confirmation of dust collector alarm state for EQ-P2-L1-SB03 and the exact text of the alarm condition where practical.

- Communication logs between electrical and ventilation teams citing use of SOP-P2-L1-01 and SOP-P2-L1-03 as references for coordination and lockout procedures.

- Copies of energized work permits and permits to work that reference this bulletin.

- Postwork lockout removal verification and any control adjustments made as a result of resolving the alarm. Note any references to ECN-2026-036 when hardware or wiring changes were involved.

Effective date
--------------

Effective immediately. All work planning and permits for the induction power cabinet area and for shot blast cabinet ventilation must comply with this bulletin and with the procedures cited below. Refer to SOP-P2-L1-01 and SOP-P2-L1-03 for detailed procedures and to ECN-2026-036 for recent engineering change information that may affect implementation.

References
----------

ECN-2026-036  
SOP-P2-L1-01  
SOP-P2-L1-03

Contact
-------

Maintenance engineering and the electrical safety officer on site should be consulted for interpretation and for assistance with implementation of controls described in this bulletin.
